record.summary: Nandini Rao runs Kaveri Kitchen, a home‑based packaged‑spice business that started selling at local markets in 2019 and moved to online sales in 2021. She uses a logo of a stylised copper pot with a leaf on her packaging, social media and market‑stall banners, but never registered the mark. In March 2024 she received a legal notice from Kaveri Foods Pvt. Ltd., which filed a trademark for a similar pot logo (without a leaf) in 2024. The notice demands that she stop using the logo, destroy existing packaging and pay a penalty within 15 days. Nandini claims she used the logo years before the company’s filing, that the marks are only superficially similar, and that there has been no customer confusion. She is worried about the bulk packaging she has just reordered and wants to know if prior use gives her any rights, whether she can challenge the registration, whether she should rebrand, and how to respond to the notice.
record.goal: Seek advice on trademark rights based on prior use, possible challenges to the opponent’s registration, options on rebranding, and appropriate response to the cease‑and‑desist notice.
questions: Do you know the exact filing date (day and month) of Kaveri Foods Pvt. Ltd.'s trademark registration in 2024?
On which exact date (day) did you receive the legal notice in March 2024?
Do you have any written records (e.g., dated sketches, design drafts, or earlier marketing material) that pre‑date 2019 and show the same logo?
Have you ever received any complaint, misdirected order, or indication of actual confusion from customers or third parties regarding the two logos?
Would you be open to rebranding your business if the legal risk remains high, or do you prefer to pursue a challenge to the opponent’s registration?
evidence: Photographs of 2019 market stall showing the logo on the banner.
2020 invoices from a local printer for logo‑printed labels.
Instagram posts from 2020 onward showing the packaging.
Customer testimonial from 2020 mentions the logo by description but not by image.
Online order records from 2021 with sales figures.
Company's registration certificate dated 2024 covering spices and condiments.
Legal notice received in March 2024 demanding compliance within 15 days.

follow_up.question: Who was using the property just before the dispute?
follow_up.why: Actual possession and claimed ownership are different questions.

evidence_plan.heading: Evidence plan
prompts: Which part of the timeline needs independent support?
What already shows that event, and who may lawfully hold another record?

suggestions.title: Possession, title and notices
suggestions.look_for: Gather records you already hold, such as agreements, deeds, orders, rent payments or notices. Note who occupied the property and when that changed.
suggestions.why: Documents and the timeline can help distinguish possession from a claim about legal ownership.
suggestions.action: Keep full copies and record where each came from. Request records through the issuing office or a lawyer when needed.

suggestions.title: Location and visible changes
suggestions.look_for: Note the address or boundary reference and any changed lock, barrier or damage you actually observed.
suggestions.why: This helps identify the location and the particular change in dispute.
suggestions.action: Document only from an area you may safely and lawfully access. Do not enter disputed space or confront anyone.

suggestions.title: Original records and an evidence log
suggestions.look_for: Keep records you lawfully have, with their surrounding context. For each item note the related event, who provided it, when you received it, and any transfer.
suggestions.why: The log distinguishes what you observed from what someone later told you and makes it easier to check the source.
suggestions.action: Keep an unchanged original and label working copies. Avoid editing originals, guessing gaps, or sharing evidence publicly.
